title: Flesh-eating screwworms feast on humans in Mexico; human cases top 500
excerpt: Six deaths reported among screwworm cases, one directly attributed to the flies.
content_html:
The study identified 204 cases in all, but two did not have sufficient data to be included in the analysis. Of the 202 remaining cases, researchers found 145 (72 percent) were in male patients. The age of fly victims ranged from 12 to 93 years, but skewed toward older adults, with a mean of 61. Most of the myiasis cases (77 percent) were in patients with one or more underlying health conditions, most commonly diabetes, alcoholism, cancers, and skin conditions.

When the flies infect humans, they seem to have the most success infesting the legs and feet, the study found; More than half (55 percent) of cases were in the lower limbs. But the flies are not picky. The next most common sites were reported as the head/neck, including the nose, mouth, and eyes. Fewer cases were seen in the upper limbs, trunk, ear, genitalia, and abdominal cavity.

Six deaths were reported among patients with confirmed NWS myiasis, but it’s unclear in most of the cases how much the infestation contributed to the deaths. Only one had NWS myiasis listed as the cause of the death. The other deaths were in patients with cancers, encephalitis, respiratory failure, and septic shock. The average age of patients with NWS-linked deaths was 79.5 years.

One Health approach

The geographic distribution of the human cases unsurprisingly mirrored the distribution of reported animal cases. But it remains unclear why men seem to be at higher risk of the flesh-eating maggots. They speculated that occupational exposure, outdoor activities, contact with animals, unattended wounds, or delayed healthcare seeking could be factors in the imbalance.

Overall, the researchers conclude that the cases highlight an important link between human and animal health.

“Because animal and human cases reflect northward spread of the NWS fly and that spread is expected to continue, surveillance, diagnostic preparedness, animal movement controls, and fly-suppression activities should be implemented proactively at the leading edge of expansion, rather than only after human cases are detected,” the researchers write. “Coordination between human health, animal health, wildlife, and agricultural sectors will be essential to guide prevention and control measures.”

The US reported its first animal cases in Texas in June amid the reemergence. Since then, the USDA has reported 45 animal cases. So far, no human NWS myiasis cases have been reported in the US from the fly’s resurgence. But there have been travel-related cases amid the reemergence in Central America and from people returning from other locations with endemic NWS populations.

content_html_zh:
该研究总共确定了 204 个案例，但其中两个案例没有足够的数据进行分析。 研究人员发现，在剩下的 202 例病例中，有 145 例（72%）是男性患者。 苍蝇受害者的年龄从 12 岁到 93 岁不等，但以老年人为主，平均年龄为 61 岁。 大多数蝇蛆病病例（77%）是患有一种或多种潜在健康状况的患者，最常见的是糖尿病、酗酒、癌症和皮肤病。

研究发现，当苍蝇感染人类时，它们似乎最成功地感染腿和脚；超过一半（55%）的病例发生在下肢。 但苍蝇并不挑剔。 据报道，第二常见的部位是头部/颈部，包括鼻子、嘴巴和眼睛。 上肢、躯干、耳部、生殖器、腹腔等部位病例较少。

据报道，确诊的 NWS 蝇蛆病患者中有 6 人死亡，但在大多数病例中，尚不清楚感染对死亡的影响有多大。 只有一例的死亡原因被列为 NWS 蝇蛆病。 其他死亡病例是患有癌症、脑炎、呼吸衰竭和感染性休克的患者。 NWS 相关死亡患者的平均年龄为 79.5 岁。

一种健康方法

毫不奇怪，人类病例的地理分布反映了报告的动物病例的分布。 但目前尚不清楚为什么男性似乎更容易感染食肉蛆。 他们推测，职业暴露、户外活动、与动物接触、伤口无人处理或延迟就医可能是造成这种不平衡的因素。

总的来说，研究人员得出的结论是，这些病例凸显了人类和动物健康之间的重要联系。

研究人员写道：“由于动物和人类病例反映了 NWS 蝇向北传播，并且这种传播预计将持续下去，因此应在传播的前沿主动实施监测、诊断准备、动物运动控制和蝇抑制活动，而不是仅在发现人类病例后才进行。” “人类健康、动物健康、野生动物和农业部门之间的协调对于指导预防和控制措施至关重要。”

六月，美国在德克萨斯州报告了首例动物病例，当时该病例再次出现。 此后，美国农业部报告了 45 起动物病例。 到目前为止，美国尚未报告因这种苍蝇死灰复燃而造成的人类 NWS 蝇蛆病病例。 但在中美洲重新出现疫情以及从其他 NWS 人群流行地区返回的人们中，出现了与旅行相关的病例。
